content: Coxsackievirus is a cytolytic virus belonging to the Picornaviridae family and is classified as an enterovirus. Enteroviruses include polioviruses, coxsackieviruses, and echoviruses. Among the 61 non-polio enteroviruses that can cause disease in humans, 23 are Coxsackie A viruses, and 6 are Coxsackie B viruses. Enteroviruses are the second most common viral infectious agents in humans, following rhinoviruses. Coxsackieviruses are divided into two main groups: Coxsackie A viruses and Coxsackie B viruses. Coxsackie B viruses consist of six serotypes, one of which is Coxsackie B4, a clinically significant serotype. Both Coxsackie A and B viruses are capable of causing a wide range of diseases in humans. These diseases can be differentiated based on the organ systems involved, clinical presentation, and diagnostic techniques. For example, oral lesions caused by Coxsackievirus must be distinguished from other oral conditions such as oral candidiasis and aphthous ulcers. Oral lesions associated with Coxsackievirus infections should also be differentiated from other diseases that cause similar lesions, such as leukoplakia and herpes simplex virus infections.
